limitations: Only the eight manifest-referenced saved whole images were opened, each exactly once via view_image. No reopens, crops, derived images, other images, browser/native calls, or runtime checks were used.

Whole-view scaling is a review constraint, not evidence that the native application uses tiny fonts. Explicit tool resizing occurred for desktop answers (1440x8360 to 1033x6000), mobile answers (390x11413 to 205x6000), and mobile choices (390x6319 to 370x6000).

Tall whole images allow inspection of overall wrapping, containment, spacing, and visible gross collisions, but do not establish every exact glyph, subscript, superscript, sign, fraction detail, punctuation mark, or reading comfort at original size. The strongest fine-glyph limit is the reduced mobile answers image.

Static selectors and navigation buttons do not prove click or selection behavior, submission, feedback states, scrolling, touch-target size, keyboard navigation, focus behavior, screen-reader semantics, accessibility compliance, or live rendering across other viewports.

No DOM report, source textbook, lesson source, science calculation, or independent content/choice review artifact was consulted. The user's reported independent content/choice PASS is contextual only and is not repeated as this review's approval.
Answer 4 was inspected for visible paragraph containment and wrapping on both answer images, not for exact repaired wording or source/science correctness.
The inputs array preserves the complete images array from inputs.json, including its supplied byte counts and hashes. Image identity metadata was not independently rehashed.
This PASS applies only to observable display defects in these bounded saved pixels. It is not general product acceptance or approval of unseen states.
